stories.headline: Moth swarms that once blocked out the stars are back
stories.summary: Drought, pesticides and habitat loss wiped out an estimated 99.5% of Australia's Bogong moths after 2017. This spring, scientists are seeing big migrating swarms again, likely helped by wetter weather.
stories.why: The moths pollinate plants and feed the critically endangered mountain pygmy possum.

stories.stat_label: sq ft teaching complex with mosaics
stories.headline: The likely school of Aristotle and Alexander emerges
stories.summary: At Mieza, archaeologists found lecture rooms with stone benches and a 1,700 sq ft complex with mosaic floors at the royal gymnasium where Aristotle is believed to have taught a young Alexander the Great.
stories.why: It's a rare glimpse of the place that shaped one of history's most famous students.

stories.headline: One of the rarest cats on Earth shows up on a camera trap
stories.summary: A remote camera near La Payunia Reserve caught the elusive Andean cat, the 'ghost of the Andes', crossing rocky slopes. It's the 3rd sighting since 2024 on land being restored for wildlife.
stories.why: It's a sign that years of habitat restoration are working for one of the most endangered cats.

stories.headline: Stem-cell heart patches reach their 1st patient after approval
stories.summary: Surgeons in Japan placed sheets of heart muscle cells made from iPS stem cells on the heart of a woman in her 50s, the world's first surgery using the newly approved, commercially made sheets.
stories.why: Stem-cell science behind a 2012 Nobel Prize is now reaching people with failing hearts.

stories.stat_label: wild baby for a rescued orphan
stories.headline: A gorilla rescued from traffickers has her first wild baby
stories.summary: Lulingu was rescued at 18 months old and raised at the GRACE sanctuary. Released on Mount Tshiaberimu in 2024, she joined a wild silverback's group and gave birth in May.
stories.why: The tiny group there was at risk of dying out without new breeding females.

stories.headline: Crew-13 makes the fastest US trip ever to the space station
stories.summary: SpaceX's Dragon reached the ISS just 7 hours 55 minutes after launch, a US record. The last crew took over 30 hours. Commander Jessica Watkins is the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit.
stories.why: Faster trips mean less time cramped in a capsule, and a historic first for the crew.

stories.headline: A snake missing since 1872 turns up on a road in India
stories.summary: A forest patrol near Bhuj photographed an Afro-Asian sand snake, the first confirmed record in Kutch in over 150 years. The last specimens were collected by naturalist Ferdinand Stoliczka in 1871–72.
stories.why: It links a 19th-century record to today, proof that dry, overlooked landscapes still hide wildlife.
stories.stat_label: last record of it in Kutch

stories.headline: A bird lost for 13 years is filmed for the first time
stories.summary: Crossing a small rainforest bridge, two bird surveyors spotted a yellow, orange and black Ghana cuckooshrike, unseen since 2013, and took the first known video of it on a 6-month West Africa trip.
stories.why: Experts say the photos may be the best ever taken of this bird.

fun_fact: Bogong moth swarms once showed up on radar at the Sydney 2000 Olympics, mistaken for rain.
